![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/ca5253e78d49779f7ab269e2fd55143b:32d79d0bf6a0e148784d3b1ce0064dad/arthur-mensch-gradient-1536x1536-v1.webp)

Arthur Mensch, CEO & Co-Founder of Mistral AI

Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch is building sovereign, open-weight AI models for European enterprise after a record €3bn Series D led by Samsung Electronics

Three years after launch, [Mistral AI](https://aimagazine.com/company/mistral) has closed the largest equity round ever raised by a European tech company.

Samsung Electronics led the €3bn (US$3.4bn) Series D in September 2026, valuing the Paris lab at more than €21bn (US$23.5bn), with ASML and NVIDIA already on the cap table.

With a trillion-parameter Mistral Large 4 in preview, a data centre south of Paris and more than 125 enterprise customers, it has become Europe's clearest answer to the US frontier labs.

[Arthur Mensch](https://aimagazine.com/executive/arthur-mensch), Co-founder and CEO of Mistral AI, has previously said: “Open frontier models are how AI becomes a true platform.”

Paris’s AI efforts are pioneered by Mistral, Europe’s biggest AI company. Credit: Getty

## What is Mistral AI?

Mistral was [founded in Paris](https://aimagazine.com/news/europe-paris-outpaces-london-as-europes-top-ai-city) in 2023 by Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix, researchers from Google DeepMind and Meta.

From the start, it bet on open-weight models that companies can run on their own infrastructure, and on a promise of [European control](https://aimagazine.com/ai-applications/snowflake-mistral-ai-partner-to-democratise-business-ai) over data and technology often referred to as ‘sovereign AI’. The funding curve has steepened sharply. ASML led a €1.7bn (US$1.9bn) Series C in September 2025 at €11.7bn (US$13.1bn).

A year later, the Series D nearly doubled that valuation. Revenue is growing too. The company reported revenue in 2026: an annualised run rate above $400 million in February.

Its customer list leans towards regulated and industrial Europe, where data control matters most. Airbus, ASML and HSBC are among more than 125 global enterprises in 20 countries. HSBC signed a multi-year deal in December 2025 to run self-hosted Mistral models across the bank. Arthur said at the time: “We are proud to engage in this long-term partnership with HSBC.”

TotalEnergies runs a joint innovation lab, and CMA CGM is deploying Mistral among thousands of employees.

![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/bEt4wczgGR8/hqdefault.jpg)

> Open frontier models are how AI becomes a true platform
>
> Arthur Mensch, Co-founder and CEO of Mistral AI

## LLMs and hardware

The product range now spans the stack. Mistral Large 4, previewed in October 2026, has one trillion parameters, 52bn of them active, and was trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs.

Mistral Compute offers regional inference for customers who need data to stay in Europe. A 44MW data centre at Bruyères-le-Chtel is designed for about 13,800 [NVIDIA GB300 GPUs](https://aimagazine.com/news/why-nvidia-is-backing-britains-ai-safety-with-us-250m-push).

[Mistral AI](https://datacentremagazine.com/company/mistral) raised US$830m in [debt financing](https://datacentremagazine.com/news/how-mistral-ai-is-advancing-ai-infrastructure-in-europe) to support the construction of a new data centre near Paris, adding to a growing pipeline of AI infrastructure across Europe.

Mistral plans up to 1GW of compute in Europe by 2030, is co-developing open frontier models with NVIDIA through the Nemotron Coalition, and has signed a deal worth hundreds of millions of euros with Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN.

Mistral’s powerful AI platform is expected to provide Samsung with a [unique stack](https://aimagazine.com/articles/totalenergies-mistral-advancing-ai-energy-transition) of tools that will transform how semiconductors are designed and manufactured.

Mistral has turned European sovereignty from a policy talking point into a business. Banks, shipping lines and energy groups are choosing it because they can run its models inside their own walls, and its investors span the hardware supply chain.

Mistral AI in numbers

* Series D: €3bn (US$3.4bn) at more than €21bn (US$23.5bn) post-money on 8 September 2026, led by Samsung Electronics
* Valuation growth: up from €11.7bn (US$13.1bn) after the €1.7bn (US$1.9bn) Series C led by ASML in September 2025
* Customers: more than 125 global enterprises in 20 countries (September 2026)
* Mistral Large 4: one trillion parameters with 52bn active, previewed in October 2026

## Top technology partners

* [**Samsung Electronics**](https://aimagazine.com/company/samsung-electronics)**:** Led the €3bn (US$3.4bn) Series D. Under the agreement, Samsung will integrate Mistral’s AI services and solutions — including its flagship large language model, Mistral Large – across its semiconductor operations to develop customised on-premises AI models optimised for intelligence-driven infrastructure.
* [**ASML**](https://aimagazine.com/company/asml-holding)**:** The Dutch lithography leader led Mistral's Series C. The two are exploring AI for semiconductor equipment and engineering, and ASML backs Mistral's European compute programme.
* [**NVIDIA**](https://aimagazine.com/company/nvidia)**:**An investor and a founding member alongside Mistral of the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition, announced in March 2026. The pair will co-develop open frontier models, starting with a base model on DGX Cloud that underpins NVIDIA's Nemotron 4 family.
* [**Microsoft**](https://aimagazine.com/company/microsoft)**:** Mistral expanded its partnership with Microsoft in summer 2026 to add compute capacity in Europe, supporting demand for its models from enterprises that need their data to stay inside the region.
* [**HUMAIN**](https://www.humain.com): A collaboration worth hundreds of millions of euros, announced in August 2026, to build Arabic-strong frontier models, deploy AI in Saudi Arabia's regulated industries and explore HUMAIN's data centres, starting with cybersecurity and voice.

# Mistral says its new model, Large 4, achieves ‘frontier’ performance among open models for agentic coding and cyber defense

![Arthur Mensch, founder of Mistral AI.](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/GettyImages-2198382126-e1793276967802.jpg?format=webp&w=1440&quality=75)

[French AI lab Mistral](https://fortune.com/2026/08/05/mistral-europe-ai-sovereignty-us-openai-anthropic-google-deepmind/) has released it’s newest model, Mistral Large 4, to the public—claiming it has chased its Chinese rivals to the frontier of open-weight AI.

Unlike most leading AI models, open-weight models are made freely available for anyone to download, run and modify. It is a class of AI models where the leading products have traditionally come from China-based companies.

The French startup says its new 1 trillion-parameter model, available on open-source platform Hugging Face from Thursday, is the best open model built in the West. Mistral says it narrowly tops all other open models on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an independent benchmark that measures how well AI agents complete full software engineering tasks.

According to benchmark figures provided by Mistral, the new model ties with China’s GLM-5.3, previously considered to be the best open model in the world, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, a test of coding agents. The company said that additional reinforcement learning training it has conducted since releasing a preview version of Large 4 on Oct. 6 has allowed the model’s performance on Terminal Bench 4.0 to jump from 28% accuracy to 41% accuracy. Proprietary models from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, which can only be accessed through an API, remain ahead in overall capabilities. For instance, Anthropic’s Mythos 5.1 scored 60.9% on the same benchmark.

Mistral said, however, that Large 4 is also much more efficient than its Chinese open weight rivals, using 47% fewer tokens per task than GLM-5.3.

Large 4, which Mistral often refers to as “Le Chonk,” a humorous French wordplay based around the company’s cat mascot, was previously released as a limited preview with select partners. At that stage, Artificial Analysis rated it roughly on par with OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek’s V4.1 Flash, but found it cost more than four times as much per task as open models of similar intelligence.  
  
Pierre Stock, Mistral’s vice president of science, attributed the fresh gains the company is now reporting for the full release of Large 4 to three more weeks of reinforcement learning, a training method in which a model gets feedback on its attempts at tasks and learns to favor the approaches that work.

Stock called the release “a pivotal moment in the global AI race” and “a turning point for Europe,” arguing the continent can now build an ecosystem around AI foundation models, “not only the application layer.” He said the model was trained on Mistral’s own 10-megawatt computing cluster in France, “a fraction of what all the competitors use.”

Stock said the model was now “the best open-weight model on cyber in particular and coding.” He also suggested that Mistral’s model should be the defualt for companies and questioned whether Chinese open models can be trusted. Chinese models may be subject to future export controls, he said. He also said that a model’s behavior could be tweaked to exfiltrate secrets from a company’s systems.

Open-weight models are gaining ground with businesses who are attracted by the lower cost of these models and the greater ability for control over the data they process. Stock said “business continuity” is the top request from customers in finance, manufacturing and other regulated industries, such as healthcare, who worry that access to closed models “can be cut off.”

That risk was most keenly felt in June, when a U.S. export-control directive forced Anthropic to suspend access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for nearly three weeks. Stock argued that once a model’s weights are public “it’s impossible to cut off access” in this way.   
  
In addition, he said open models were essential for cyber defense, as closed models may rate-limit users or refuse legitimate requests to probe their own systems for vulnerabilities or engage in anti-hacking activities because of a similarity with some offensive cyber tasks.

In July, after OpenAI models breached Hugging Face’s servers during testing, Hugging Face’s team tried to respond using Anthropic’s Opus and Fable models. Those models refused much of the work because of their safety guardrails, and the team switched to an open model from China’s Z.ai.

Mistral was founded in Paris in April 2023 by Arthur Mensch, a former Google DeepMind researcher, and Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix, who both came from [Meta](https://fortune.com/company/facebook/). It has released open models since its first one, Mistral 7B, came out later that year. The company has struggled to keep pace with U.S. labs, with its models generally trailing the top American systems.

It also faces an enormous funding gap. Mistral has raised roughly $6 billion in three years, most recently a €3 billion Series D in September led by [Samsung](https://fortune.com/company/samsung-electronics/), which valued the company at more than €21 billion (about $24 billion). Anthropic was valued at $965 billion as of August.

Beatrice Nolan is a tech reporter on *Fortune*’s AI team, covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and their impact on work, industry, and culture. She's based in *Fortune*'s London office and holds a bachelor’s degree in English from the University of York. You can reach her securely via Signal at beatricenolan.08

# Mistral’s New ‘Le Chonk’ AI Model Is Big, Open and Now Available for Download

Mistral Large 4 is a state-of-the-art model for cyberdefense, manufacturing, finance-related tasks and multimodal use.

![](https://www.cnet.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/069e3ec3-6c74-47a6-a0e2-512f830cf4ce.jpg?w=80)

Reporter II

#### Macy Meyer

Reporter II

October 29, 2026, 1:32 pm ET

![Mistral Large 4](https://www.cnet.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/Screenshot-2026-10-06-at-2.38.54-PM.png?w=826)

New AI models are coming, and they don’t stop coming.

On the heels of the recent rollouts of [Meta’s Muse](https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/meta-muse-ai-agent-personal-computer-2026-news/) and [Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon](https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/google-genie-4-gemini-4-carbon-ai-news/), Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, [Mistral Large 4](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/). The model – affectionately known as “Le Chonk” – was [available in public preview](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4/) earlier this month. Now, after weeks of additional reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and assessing it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials, the Mistral team announced Thursday that ML4 is available for download.

“The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations,” Mistral said in its announcement. “We’ve put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity.”

More from CNET

A French company known for its open-source and open-weight LLMs, Mistral AI reports that the Large 4 model “ranks among the best open-weight models of the world” on aggregated metrics and also outperforms European and US models, while also catching up to Chinese competitors, who have been dominating the open-weight sector.

Earlier this month, I spoke with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – what they’re calling the best open model built in the West – and its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.

## Key capabilities of Mistral Large 4

Lample and Stock said that Mistral Large 4 was built to process both text and images, closing performance gaps from previous Mistral models. Specifically, Large 4 touts more advanced cybersecurity and agentic capabilities, as well as a better ability to handle manufacturing- and finance-related tasks.

### Cybersecurity

Mistral Large 4 was designed to excel at defensive cybersecurity tasks, including log inspection, code auditing and checking for newly published exploits or vulnerabilities. Beyond defensive measures, Mistral says the new model offers offensive cybersecurity measures to identify and address weaknesses.

### Agentic AI

“Really, the core competency we’re looking at for ML4 is agentic capabilities,” Stock said.

Mistral Large 4 was built with a focus on [agentic](https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/what-is-agentic-ai-everything-to-know-about-artificial-intelligence-agents/) performance for planning, research or handling complex enterprise tasks that would take human experts hours or days to complete. The Mistral AI team said the model reaches “state-of-the-art” performance on critical agentic benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal Bench – evaluation frameworks for testing how well agents handle complex tasks – for tasks like coding, analyzing and pulling requests.

### Geospatial and grounding capabilities

Mistral says the model outperforms competitors in aerial and satellite imagery analysis, with the capacity to identify visual patterns and objects on maps, such as [forest fires](https://www.cnet.com/science/climate/wildfires-are-raging-across-the-world-how-nasa-is-using-satellite-data-to-fight-back/).

“On grounding capabilities, it outperforms all existing models, including the closed ones,” Mistral said when it released the model preview. “These are critical as cyberattacks get faster and cheaper, companies write more code than ever and the world needs more chips to keep up with AI demand.”

Grounding is a technique used in AI development to try to eliminate [hallucinations](https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/what-are-ai-hallucinations-why-chatbots-make-things-up-and-what-you-need-to-know/) – when the LLM generates inaccurate information – by anchoring the AI’s outputs in external resources, like documents and databases, rather than just the materials it was trained on internally. Grounding also helps keep data and information fresh while providing context for the AI’s responses.

Mistral says the new model was also trained on more than 160 languages, including every official language of the European Union, as well as Latin and non-Latin languages, to answer prompts natively.

If you’re interested in getting started with ML4, it’s available to try and customize in [Mistral Studio](https://console.mistral.ai/home), through the Mistral [API](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0#use-mistral-large-4-0), or on [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/mistralai/mistral-large-4-0). Mistral also says you can download the open weights from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B), try ML4 in [Vibe Code](https://chat.mistral.ai/code?model=mistral-large-4-0) or access it through [Nvidia-hosted endpoints](https://build.nvidia.com/mistralai/mistral-large-4-1t-a52b), with additional options to customize for enterprise users.

## **CERN and Mistral join forces to accelerate AI for science**

CERN and Mistral sign a statement of intent to advance AI for science and strengthen Europe’s scientific and technological capabilities

—

![](https://home.cern/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CERN_Mistral-scaled.png)

CERN and Mistral join forces to advance AI for science (Image: CERN / Mistral)

CERN, the European Laboratory for Particle Physics, and Mistral, a European developer of large-scale AI models, have signed a statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership focused on developing foundation models for scientific discovery.

The partnership brings together CERN’s expertise in fundamental physics, scientific data and large-scale computing with Mistral’s leadership in large-scale model training, leveraging these combined capabilities and resources to advance AI for science on an exceptional scale. While the initial focus is on high-energy physics, the partnership has the potential to contribute to the development of AI approaches that can serve the broader scientific community.

At the heart of this work is the ambition to develop a single pretrained Large Physics Model – the first foundation model for collider physics. It will be trained on billions of simulated proton-proton collisions at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world’s largest and most powerful particle accelerator, and designed to support multiple tasks, from reconstructing particle collisions and identifying particles to flagging unexpected signals and evaluating future detector designs.

The model is intended to address a fundamental challenge in analysing LHC collisions. Today, reconstruction relies on a chain of specialised algorithms that progressively transform detector signals into the particles and other objects used for physics analysis. Machine learning has long played an important role in this process, improving performance across a range of specialised tasks. Foundation models offer the potential to build on these advances, learning across the whole reconstruction chain and supporting multiple tasks within a single model.

“High-energy physics provides a unique environment in which artificial intelligence can be developed and tested with exceptional rigour. We are partnering with Mistral, a leading European AI company, to advance AI capabilities that can serve the whole physics community and be shared,” said Enrica Porcari, CERN’s Chief Information Officer.

CERN is home to one of the world’s largest volumes of scientific data, with around one exabyte – one million terabytes – of experimental data from the LHC stored to date. The number of collisions is set to increase tenfold with the HL-LHC, which is expected to begin operation around 2030. This combination of scale and scientific precision provides exceptional conditions for developing and testing AI.

“We are proud to work with CERN to explore what large-scale AI models can bring to the growing complexity of particle physics. Together, we have the opportunity to push the frontiers of high-energy physics, developing AI capabilities that have the potential to lead to new scientific discoveries,”said Johannes Brandstetter, Vice-President of AI for Engineering at Mistral.

By bringing together European excellence in AI and fundamental science, this partnership marks a step towards a new generation of AI tools capable of addressing the scale, precision and complexity of modern science in Europe and beyond.

**About Mistral:**

Mistral is a global AI lab building state-of-the-art open-weight models, products and infrastructure that enable enterprises, public institutions and advanced industries to own, customise and control their AI. Headquartered in France, Mistral has a strong international presence across Europe, North America and Asia.

For more information, visit [www.mistral.ai](http://www.mistral.ai/).

# Mistral Releases 1-Trillion-Parameter AI Model for Cybersecurity

Mistral releases Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight AI model targeting cybersecurity. Here’s what IT teams should know about costs and deployment.

Written By [![](data:image/avif;base64,)
![Aminu Abdullahi](https://assets.techrepublic.com/uploads/2022/05/cropped-Aminu-2.jpg?w=64)

Aminu Abdullahi](/meet-the-team/us/aminu-abdullahi/)

Oct 30, 2026

![Mistral Releases 1-Trillion-Parameter AI Model for Cybersecurity](https://assets.techrepublic.com/uploads/2026/10/minstral.jpg?w=640)

Mistral makes Large 4 open-weight AI model publicly available. Image: Mistral

Mistral AI is giving security teams another option for running advanced AI models without relying entirely on outside cloud providers.

The French artificial intelligence developer publicly released the weights for its 1-trillion-parameter flagship model, Mistral Large 4, on Oct. 29. The move lets public agencies and private enterprises download, inspect, and host the software directly on their own hardware.

Following a three-week public preview, Mistral added focused reinforcement learning to tune the system for autonomous software development and [vulnerability management](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/top-vulnerability-management-tools/), positioning it as an open rival to closed systems from OpenAI and Google.

## Code defense meets token efficiency

Mistral Large 4 scored 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, reflecting an ability to locate software bugs, reproduce them in sandboxes, and patch source code without breaking features.

The company noted that the model blocks malicious requests with a 96.6% refusal rate while remaining accessible to security analysts performing legitimate administrative audits.

In software engineering benchmarks, the model reached 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, edging out [China’s open-weight GLM-5.3](https://www.eweek.com/ja/news/zai-glm-5-3-coding-cybersecurity-benchmarks-china-apac/). On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 tied GLM-5.3 with a 48% score while consuming 47% fewer computational tokens per task.

“I’m not comfortable living in a world in which open weights do not exist,” Pierre Stock, Mistral’s vice president of science, [told Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/mistral-ai-publicly-releases-large-4-targets-cybersecurity-users-2026-10-29/). Stock noted to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/mistral-releases-weights-for-its-trillion-parameter-ai-model-targeting-cybersecurity/) that open weights ensure organizations retain frontier intelligence to defend against attacks without the risk of an external provider pulling the plug.

## The autonomy paradox in cyber infrastructure

Delivering frontier [security tools](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/best-penetration-testing-tools/) via downloadable weights alters enterprise software governance, shifting the barrier from access restrictions to operational competence.

When organizations host an open-weight defensive engine in-house, they bypass cloud API logging, eliminate third-party data inspection, and protect confidential code repositories from external surveillance.

Yet unlike a hosted commercial service with continuous cloud-side moderation, an open model relies entirely on the operator to deploy patches and configure internal firewalls. The exact freedom that immunizes companies against [geopolitical service cutoffs and foreign vendor policies](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-china-us-drone-export-tech-restrictions-apac/) forces internal security teams to shoulder absolute operational accountability.

### More must-read AI coverage

* [SS&C Intralinks DealCentre AI vs. Datasite: Which platform is built for the future of dealmaking?](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/dealcentre-ai-vs-datasite/)
* [SS&C Intralinks FundCentre AI vs. Juniper Square: Which platform better supports modern private markets fund managers?](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/fundcentre-ai-vs-juniper-square/)
* [Why Data, Not Models, Determines AI Success](https://www.techrepublic.com/sponsored/why-data-not-models-determines-ai-success/)
* [The Rise of the AI-Native Factory: How Physical AI Is Transforming Manufacturing](https://www.eweek.com/a/artificial-intelligence/the-rise-of-the-ai-native-factory-how-physical-ai-is-transforming-manufacturing/)

## How Mistral Large 4 impacts tech and security teams

For developers, IT leaders, and security practitioners, the release creates both immediate operational savings and distinct deployment challenges:

* **Sovereignty without vendor lock-in:** Enterprises in heavily regulated sectors can host the software on-premises or via local clouds, eliminating the risk of sudden policy shutdowns or sensitive data exposure through foreign APIs.
* **Cost reductions in coding workflows:** Running agentic workflows with 47% fewer tokens per task significantly cuts operational costs for corporate engineering pipelines running high-volume terminal workloads.
* **Heavy hardware requirements:** Running a 1-trillion-parameter model, even one with sparse parameter activation, demands significant on-premises [GPU infrastructure](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-intel-xeon-rack-designs-d-series-gpu-ai/), pricing out smaller shops without specialized hardware or cloud partners.
* **Dual-use exposure:** Open weights cannot be remotely recalled once distributed. Organizations face an environment where automated exploitation and vulnerability analysis become widely accessible across both sides of the cybersecurity spectrum.

The weights are available immediately on Hugging Face, alongside cloud access through Mistral’s commercial API, NVIDIA NIM containers, and Microsoft Foundry. Mistral lists API pricing at $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens, with cached input costing $0.07 per million tokens.

Before deploying Mistral Large 4, IT teams should assess whether their infrastructure can support the model’s memory and computing requirements, along with the costs of hosting and maintaining it.

Security teams should also test the model against their own vulnerability management workflows, establish approval requirements for AI-generated code changes, and confirm that access controls and logging meet organizational policies.

Benchmark performance can help narrow the options, but real-world testing is necessary to determine whether the model delivers reliable results for an organization’s specific security tasks.

**Other news: [Discord is preparing to make messages from eligible public servers](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-discord-messages-web-search-privacy-settings/) searchable on the web, raising new privacy concerns for users and community administrators.**

## The French AI company says its Large 4 model offers advanced coding and cyber-defence capabilities and can be run on an organisation’s own computers and servers.

Mistral has [released the weights for its latest large flagship AI model](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/), Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed “Le Chonk”, claiming improvements in coding and cyber defence as Europe seeks to build alternatives to US and Chinese technology.

![](/images/logos/logo-euronews-stacked-outlined-72x72-grey-9.svg)
![](/images/logos/logo-euronews-stacked-outlined-72x72-grey-9.svg)

The French firm claims the model is “the best open agentic coding model in the world”, offering enterprises and governments “frontier AI cyber defence capabilities they can fully own and control” including the ability to “detect, analyse and respond to cyberthreats across code and IT infrastructure".

The release follows a [preview of ML4 on 6 October](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/06/what-to-know-about-mistrals-ml4-as-it-bets-on-eu-sovereignty-in-the-us-china-open-weight-a). Since then, Mistral has spent the last three weeks reinforcing the model's learning, testing it with customers and partners under real-world conditions.

“ML4 OSS showcases our science team's ability to innovate at speed. Building on the ML4 Preview, the open weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation," said Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral.

"In under three weeks within the same reinforcement learning run, we integrated customer feedback by introducing two additional reasoning modes, while making ML4 more efficient and customisable,” he added.

Mistral says the latest release of ML4 rivals other leading open models for coding while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average than Chinese model GLM-5.3. Its score on Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests AI agents’ ability to perform coding tasks in a terminal, also rose from 28% to 41% following further training.

The release also comes as Europe faces growing cybersecurity threats, such as the recent [PHP programming security flaw](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/22/websites-go-dark-after-ai-exposes-major-programming-language-security-flaw), discovered using AI, as well as the recent cyber-attacks on the [Belgian](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/28/belgiums-finance-and-tax-agency-hit-by-cyberattack) and [Norwegian](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/27/norway-says-successful-cyberattacks-against-the-country-have-tripled-in-last-six-months) governments.

**More control over AI**

Making the model’s weights available allows organisations to download and run it on their own infrastructure, rather than relying exclusively on an external provider’s hosted service.

This could be particularly useful for companies handling sensitive information, such as proprietary software code, that they do not want to share with an external AI service.

Organisations would have greater control over where the model runs and how it is integrated into their systems, although they would still need suitable hardware and expertise to operate it securely.

Mistral says organisations running ML4 on their own infrastructure would also not face the risk of a third-party provider restricting access to or disabling the model.

The move comes amid concerns about European dependence on US AI providers. In June, the [Trump administration ordered Anthropic to suspend access](https://www.euronews.com/2026/06/13/wake-up-call-europe-reacts-to-anthropic-halting-access-to-its-fable-5-and-mythos-5-ai-mode) to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for foreign nationals.

The restrictions were subsequently lifted for Fable 5, while access to Mythos 5 remained limited to selected organisations. The episode highlighted how decisions made outside Europe can affect access to advanced AI services.

**Europe’s AI ambitions**

Europe continues to lag behind the US and China in the development of large AI models and the resources needed to build them.

Mistral is one of Europe’s leading AI developers, but its reported valuation of around $24 billion (€20.9 billion) is far below those of US rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.

Mistral argues that despite the disparity in resources, “ML4 is now the best open model built in the West”.

The model was trained on 3,800 of US company Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell GPUs at Mistral’s European data centres. The company says ML4 achieves “state-of-the-art performance” while mobilising “a fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs” such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

The model’s European infrastructure could give customers greater operational control, but its reliance on Nvidia chips illustrates Europe’s continued dependence on foreign suppliers for key parts of the AI supply chain.

"Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors," said Arthur Mensch, CEO and co-founder of Mistral.

"Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion."

"We have taken the lead globally in compute efficiency and have widened the gap between Mistral and other labs in that area. Our approach is to deliver quality science and put the results in everyone's hands," he added.

**A state-of-the-art model**

ML4 has 1.05 trillion parameters in total, but activates around 52 billion, according to Mistral. This means it does not use all its parameters for every task, helping it process requests more efficiently.

The model also offers three reasoning modes — low, medium and high — allowing users to adjust the depth of reasoning to suit the task, from everyday requests to more complex problems.

Mistral says ML4 can turn 2D blueprints into usable 3D models using computer-aided design (CAD) software, analyse large volumes of data to support financial decision-making and use satellite and aerial imagery to detect wildfires, track crop health and monitor risks to power lines.

The French firm says the release of ML4 is part of a new generation of models spanning all modalities and that they plan to release more models from this generation in the coming months.

The model is now available through Mistral’s API, while its weights can be downloaded from Hugging Face.

# Mistral AI Releases Weights of 1-Trillion-Parameter "Large 4" for Free, Opening Path to On-Premises Deployment for Enterprises

[Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com)

Mistral AI on October 29 published on Hugging Face the weights of an improved version of its 1-trillion-parameter large language model "Mistral Large 4." The model boosts coding and cyber-defense performance and improves inference efficiency. It is a multimodal model supporting more than 160 languages, and under a proprietary license permitting commercial use, enterprises and government agencies can run it on their own infrastructure. API pricing is $0.70 per million input tokens (about 110 yen) and $2.10 per million output tokens (about 330 yen). The offensive by European players prioritizing data sovereignty has become unmistakable.

##### Key Elements

![Mistral AI Releases Weights of 1-Trillion-Parameter ](https://img.biggo.com/VE1TgrvsklFYB45z3otpQZWwI-vxi9ZJePOj6cHnivs/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwLzMyY2NiN2I2LWFjZTItNGNlOC1hYjkwLTQ3NWNkNTg2ZjkyZF8xNzkzMzIyODE2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp)

French AI startup Mistral AI announced on October 29 that it has released the model weights of an improved version of its 1-trillion-parameter large language model "Mistral Large 4." The model is available on Hugging Face and can be run by enterprises and government agencies on their own infrastructure. The push by European players emphasizing sovereignty over data and computing infrastructure has become unmistakable in the open-weight market.

The company unveiled a preview version on October 6, and this release is positioned as an improved version with continued reinforcement learning since then. According to its official blog, the model substantially enhances coding and cyber-defense performance and improves inference efficiency. It is a multimodal model capable of handling images and supports more than 160 languages. It was trained from scratch on European infrastructure, according to the company. The model offers three inference modes—low, medium, and high—with high as the default.

On performance, the company says the model scored 19.7% on Cognition's proprietary benchmark "FrontierCode 2.0," taking the top spot. On the coding agent index of independent evaluator Artificial Analysis, it scored 48%, roughly on par with GLM-5.3, which is regarded as the leading open-weight model. It consumes an average of 47% fewer tokens per task, a reduction of more than 40% compared with GLM-5.3, the company explains. In the cyber domain, its rate of refusing malicious requests reached an average of 96.6%, the highest among open models measured by the company.

The license is the "Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License," a modified version of the MIT License, permitting use, modification, fine-tuning, and commercial use. Using vLLM or SGLang, the model can be run on a company's own infrastructure. API pricing per million tokens is $0.70 (about 110 yen) for input, $0.07 (about 11 yen) for cached input, and $2.10 (about 330 yen) for output. It is also available through Mistral Studio, the API, and OpenRouter.

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | 1 trillion |
| Supported languages | More than 160 (multimodal) |
| Inference modes | Low, medium, high (default: high) |
| License | Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (commercial use permitted) |
| Distribution | Hugging Face |
| API pricing (per million tokens) | Input $0.70 (about 110 yen) / cached input $0.07 (about 11 yen) / output $2.10 (about 330 yen) |

Note: Prices are reference values based on the conversion rates indicated in the source material.

Mistral is targeting enterprises and government agencies that want to retain control over their data and infrastructure. Demand is particularly strong in cybersecurity applications, where organizations do not want to entrust confidential information to external clouds. Under the EU AI Act, the European Commission imposes different obligations on providers and deployers of general-purpose AI models. It should be noted, however, that running a model in-house does not automatically lead to regulatory exemption.

In the market, a polarization is advancing between using closed models via API and obtaining weights to embed into one's own environment. Mistral has presented a European-origin option as a receptacle for the latter. For companies embedding the model into coding-assistance or defensive business systems, the reduction in token consumption translates directly into lower operating costs. On the other hand, some of the benchmarks rely on the company's own measurements or proprietary metrics, making verification by adopting companies essential for performance in actual operations.

### Mistral releases open weights for Mistral Large 4, providing sovereign control for the company’s ‘Le Chonk’ AI model

![Image 29](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b0aab96da155e611d7deba4d7b1b7632c27bf59f8448f335a1ab2e86a206dabc?s=96&r=pg)

by [Kyt Dotson](https://siliconangle.com/author/kitdotson/)

Mistral AI SAS [today announced](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/) the availability of the open weights of its frontier model Mistral Large 4, nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the company’s most capable large language model to date, [initially released](https://siliconangle.com/2026/10/06/mistral-launches-open-source-mistral-large-4-details-ai-roadmap/) in preview three weeks ago.

With 1 trillion parameters and 52 billion active parameters, ML4 is natively multimodal and has received three additional weeks of reinforcement training and customer testing. The company says it’s becoming one of the best open agentic coding models in the world, offering leading performance at a small fraction of the token cost with state-of-the-art cyber defense capabilities.

“ML4 OSS showcases our science team’s ability to innovate at speed,” said Vice President of Science Pierre Stock. “Building on the ML4 Preview, the open-weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation.”

The company trained ML4 on 3,800 Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell graphics processing units in its European data centers to achieve high-fidelity performance for tool use and coding, driven by end-to-end control of its infrastructure and the ability to optimize for hardware during model development.

Open weights mean companies can take the model and deploy it on their own hardware, within their own firewalls, and run sensitive data without exposing it to the cloud or outside parties. With Mistral’s model, companies will have a Western-developed model to compete with the multitude of ultra-large Chinese coding models on the market, such as the GLM family from Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co. Ltd. and the Kimi family from Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co. Ltd.

“Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Arthur Mensch. “Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion.”

![Image 30](https://images.siliconangle.com/blogs.dir/1/files/2026/10/terminal-bench-ml4-800x450.png)

Because of its training regimen, ML4 stands out among many other frontier models, rivaling even top models such as Chinese-built GLM-5.3 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests agentic coding in the terminal, ML4 climbed from 28% to 41%, tying GLM-5.3 as the best model for coding agents.

Mistral offers three reasoning modes for ML4: low, medium and high. Teams can use this to match reasoning depth to the task without adjusting prompts, which can be less effective, allowing reasoning to fit quick everyday tasks to deep work on extremely complex problems. This allows developers and enterprise users to control token use per task.

The company said the release of ML4 represents a new generation of Mistral models spanning all modalities. It follows the recent launch of [Voxtral 3](https://x.com/MistralAI/status/2112574615318876178), a family of voice models and voice agents. Mistral plans to continue to release additional models from this family in the coming months.

docs.title: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race | WIRED
docs.content:
# Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race

A few weeks ago, French company Mistral released an early version of its new artificial intelligence model, nicknamed Le Chonk. At the time, the company said it was the most advanced open-weight offering outside of China. After further refinement, Mistral now says Le Chonk is the “world’s best” open-weight model for automated coding and cybersecurity.

The advances, Mistral says, were made possible by feeding the model increasingly difficult cybersecurity and coding problems, which allowed the trillion-parameter Le Chonk to match or surpass models from leading Chinese labs like DeepSeek and Z.ai.

“It’s a pivotal moment in the global AI leadership race,” Pierre Stock, VP of science at Mistral, told reporters during a press briefing. “It offers frontier capabilities for enterprises and governments to defend against an increasing threat level in cyber.”

The finalized version of Le Chonk is now freely available for anybody to access. After a flurry of AI-related cybersecurity incidents, Mistral claims that it’s important for the West to have its own advanced open-weight models. “You have no guarantee that [Chinese models] won’t behave maliciously. They can be threat vectors,” Stock said.

The most high-profile episode occurred when one of OpenAI’s models broke loose from a testing sandbox and hacked into multiple companies over the summer. It sparked panic over the idea that AI could escape human oversight and be abused by threat actors to launch sophisticated cyberattacks. (One of the affected companies, Hugging Face, used an open-weight model from China to assess and defend against the attack.)

Since then, AI has unearthed security vulnerabilities in ubiquitous software, too. In October, a raft of websites were taken offline after an AI tool discovered serious flaws in a foundational piece of web technology.

Mistral pitches its open-weight models, like Le Chonk, as part of the solution. If AI is destined to become a central feature of both cyber offense and defense, the argument goes, businesses and governments will need to be equipped with models that are freely available and cannot be switched off remotely, unlike proprietary models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

“AI is going to be like electricity. You don’t want to live in a world in which your neighbor can cut off electricity from one day to another,” Stock said. “Once you open source the weights, they’re all over the internet. It’s impossible to cut off access.”

The trade-off, however, is that freely available models can also be downloaded and customized by threat actors.

“It’s clearly a dual-use technology,” Rafe Pilling, senior director of threat intelligence at security company Sophos, tells WIRED. “Anything that’s available to download and circulate unfettered has the ability to be abused as well as used for productive purposes.”

According to Pilling, though it’s possible a Chinese model with internet access could siphon away data, all advanced models are capable of going rogue without careful supervision—no matter their country of origin.

“The technical realities and the narrative—which often has a nationalistic leaning—are two different things,” he says.“It’s about having the right monitoring and controls in place to be confident that, even if the model was trying to be deceptive or nefarious, you might have some way of detecting it.”

# Orange Cyberdefense strikes Mistral AI partnership

By [Jasdip Sensi](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/author/jasdipmobileeurope-co-uk/)

-

"Pinterest")[WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Orange+Cyberdefense+strikes+Mistral+AI+partnership %0A%0A https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/orange-cyberdefense-mistral-ai/ "WhatsApp")

![](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/csm_orange_cyberdefense_partnership_mistral_ai_design_partner_mistral_large_4_chonk_967b26c290-696x396.webp "csm_orange_cyberdefense_partnership_mistral_ai_design_partner_mistral_large_4_chonk_967b26c290")

Orange Cyberdefense has partnered with [Mistral AI](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/tag/Mistral-AI/) to develop AI-powered cybersecurity tools that will help businesses detect, investigate and respond to cyber threats faster.

As a result, the partnership will give Orange Cyberdefense early access to a version of Mistral Large 4, an AI model designed to support advanced cybersecurity tasks.

The companies will initially focus on penetration testing, which identifies weaknesses in IT systems and incident investigation, helping security teams understand how [cyberattacks](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/tag/cyberattacks/) happened.

[![Sign up to our weekly newsletter](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Newsletter-aug26-mobile3.gif)](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/subscriptions/?utm_source=Content+Snippet&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=Subscribe&utm_id=Newsletter)

The aim is to use AI to speed up security operations while ensuring cybersecurity experts remain in control of important decisions.

Under the agreement, AI tools will gradually be introduced into selected Orange Cyberdefense services, helping security teams explore more potential attack scenarios, analyse evidence following incidents and establish how breaches occurred.

According to [the telecoms giant,](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/tag/Orange/) safeguards will include controlled access, activity tracking, [security](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/category/content-categories/security/) testing and human oversight, with specialists remaining responsible for critical decisions.

Orange Cyberdefense CEO, Hugues Foulon, said: “As threats become ever faster, industrialised and now automated, defense must operate at a different scale. Volume, speed, trust: these are the three challenges facing cybersecurity in the age of AI.

“With Mistral AI, we are building European cyber AI, trained by our experts and operated under their control. By combining the [power of AI](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/category/content-categories/automation-ai/), the expertise of our teams and our Cyber Threat Intelligence, we are accelerating our response so that we can protect more broadly, more quickly and with trusted European technology.”

Mistral AI Co-Founder and CTO, Timothée Lacroix, added: “We are proud to partner with Orange Cyberdefense, one of Europe’s cybersecurity leaders, and to bring them Mistral Large 4, a model with frontier capabilities in cyber. Together, we share one goal: giving European organisations a sovereign, trusted AI solution to defend themselves, built and operated in Europe.”

The partnership also focuses on European [data sovereignty](https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/tag/data-sovereignty/), with Mistral AI’s technology running on computing infrastructure based in Europe.

# France's Crédit Agricole taps Mistral AI to build its AI platform

On 20 October 2026, Crédit Agricole Artificial Intelligence announced a partnership that involves Mistral in building the group's AI platform, beyond access to its models: an agent for retail banking clients, agentic processes, and cybersecurity, presented as "a major focus". The announcements from BNP Paribas and HSBC, already partners of Mistral, do not mention cybersecurity. The announcement sets no amount, duration, model, or exclusivity.

ST**Stephane Nachez** · ·4 min

[Strategic alliance](https://www.actuia.com/type/alliance-strategique/)[Company](https://www.actuia.com/en/industry/company/)[Finance](https://www.actuia.com/en/industry/finance/)[AI in Business](https://www.actuia.com/en/topic/ai-in-business/)[Sovereignty & European AI](https://www.actuia.com/en/topic/european-ai-sovereignty/)[Security](https://www.actuia.com/en/topic/security/)

 

Illustration de l'article « Le Crédit Agricole associe Mistral à la fabrication de sa plateforme d'IA ». Visuel ActuIA généré avec l'IA.

  

Contents

File in…

Saved. Add a note?

The partnership goes beyond access to the lab's models, products, and tools. According to [the group's press release](https://www.credit-agricole.com/chaines-d-infos/toutes-les-chaines-d-info-du-groupe-credit-agricole/a-la-une/le-credit-agricole-s-allie-a-des-acteurs-europeens-de-premier-plan-pour-accelerer-le-deploiement-industriel-de-l-intelligence-artificielle), Mistral "thus contributes to the building of the AI platform" intended for all Crédit Agricole clients and employees. The projects deemed most transformative are carried out by "pooling resources from both companies". Mistral is nevertheless entering an architecture open to other providers. CA-GIP, which brings together most of the group's IT production, distributes AI computations "according to their sensitivity and criticality" between the group's private cloud, European partners, and "complementary solutions as needed".

Cybersecurity, which the release presents as "a major focus of this partnership", distinguishes the agreement from those that BNP Paribas and HSBC have signed with the same lab. According to [Bloomberg](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/mistral-developing-new-ai-model-for-banks-lacking-mythos-access), which cited anonymous sources on 13 May 2026, Mistral is developing a cybersecurity model and discussing it with European banks that do not have access to Mythos, Anthropic's restricted-access model. The Crédit Agricole release does not say whether this model is part of the agreement.

## An agent for clients, agentic processes, and cybersecurity

The 20 October release cites three workstreams: a conversational agent for clients of the group's retail banks, the "agentic transformation of key processes", and cybersecurity. Crédit Agricole Artificial Intelligence runs the group's AI foundations. With Mistral's technology, it also plans to adapt large language models to its data and use cases. The release sees this as a way to optimise performance, "and therefore the consumption of computing resources and its environmental impact".

Mistral is not the only named partner. The entity works with Prisme.AI on its internal "AI for All" programme, so that employees can use, create, and share agents within a "secure and governed" framework. It is also deploying Sécur'IA, a platform where business teams design agents connected to the information system. Sécur'IA follows Sécuri'Chat, deployed at Crédit Agricole S.A. in 2024. According to the group, nearly 9 out of 10 trained employees regularly use Sécuri'Chat.

[The version of the release published on the press site](https://presse.credit-agricole.com/le-credit-agricole-sallie-a-des-acteurs-europeens-de-premier-plan-pour-accelerer-le-deploiement-industriel-de-lintelligence-artificielle/?lang=fra) quotes Olivier Biton, director of technological transformation at Crédit Agricole S.A. He links the two agreements. According to him, they respond to "our desire to rely on French and European technology players capable of meeting the requirements of a large banking group".

## 500 million euros and a doctrine set in June

The framework dates from 10 June 2026. On that day, [Crédit Agricole announced](https://presse.credit-agricole.com/le-credit-agricole-accelere-sa-transformation-ia/?lang=fra) nearly 500 million euros of investment in AI over three years (2026-2028) and the creation of an "AI Enterprise" responsible for operating the foundations of all its entities. The text states that "the Group refuses technological dependence" and wants to "support the emergence of European technology champions". The [results release of 31 July](https://www.credit-agricole.com/pdfPreview/211049) specified that 150 million euros of this envelope is used to capitalise Crédit Agricole Artificial Intelligence. The October announcement repeats almost word for word the architecture described in June, including the distribution of computations by CA-GIP.

## BNP Paribas and HSBC, Mistral partners without a cybersecurity component

Crédit Agricole comes after two major European banks that have established a comparable relationship with Mistral. [BNP Paribas](https://group.bnpparibas/en/press-release/bnp-paribas-and-mistral-ai-extend-their-partnership-to-support-the-next-phase-of-generative-ai-deployment-within-the-group) has worked with the lab since 2023. In 2024, it signed a first group-wide contract, integrating its models into its internal LLM infrastructure. On 26 May 2026, it renewed the partnership for three years and extended it to software, solutions, and joint research projects. On the client side, the bank cites HelloïZ, the virtual assistant of Hello bank!, deployed to more than one million clients since January 2026, which it says integrates Mistral models. BNP Paribas claims a "multi-model" approach, guided by performance, data sensitivity, and geographical criteria.

[HSBC](https://www.hsbc.com/news-and-views/news/media-releases/2025/hsbc-and-mistral-ai-join-forces-to-accelerate-ai-adoption-across-global-bank) announced on 1 December 2025 a multi-year partnership with Mistral. It gives access to the lab's commercial models, including future versions, with joint development teams and self-hosted models on the bank's systems. The bank lists credit, onboarding, and anti-fraud and anti-money laundering controls among its future workstreams.

The three agreements share co-development and hosting under the bank's control. Crédit Agricole and BNP Paribas display multiple providers, HSBC says it continuously evaluates a wide range of models. The BNP Paribas and HSBC releases do not mention cybersecurity.

## No amount, duration, or named models

The 20 October release gives no amount, no commitment duration, no timeline for the client agent, and cites no particular Mistral model. It also says nothing about any exclusivity. The pattern recalls that observed with Mistral at [EDF, BMW, or Airbus](https://www.actuia.com/en/news/edf-bmw-airbus-mistral-ai-stages-its-industrial-shift-but-concrete-contracts-remain-sparse/): partnerships announced, rarely quantified. The announcement comes six weeks after [the lab's 3 billion euro fundraising](https://www.actuia.com/en/news/why-mistral-is-raising-eur3bn-from-samsung-nvidia-and-asml/).

As of 22 October, the announcement does not appear among the news published by Mistral on [its website](https://mistral.ai/news). The first verifiable milestone will be the launch of the conversational agent in the retail banks. No date has been communicated.

# Orange Cyberdefense becomes Mistral AI design partner for cybersecurity

2 November 2026, 10:12 By Editorial team

![](https://mspbusiness.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/hero-1793610710085.png)

**Orange Cyberdefense says it is the first European MSSP to join Mistral AI’s design partner programme. The company is gaining early access to a variant of Mistral Large 4 tailored to cybersecurity. Orange Cyberdefense plans to deploy the model step by step in penetration testing and incident investigation, using computing capacity within Europe.**

Orange Cyberdefense is the cybersecurity business unit of Orange Group. The company is joining the design partner programme of French AI company Mistral AI. According to Orange Cyberdefense, it is the first European managed security service provider (MSSP) in that programme. Through the partnership, the company gains early access to a variant of the Mistral Large 4 language model tailored to cybersecurity.

### Use in pentests and incident response

Orange Cyberdefense has announced that it will gradually integrate AI systems based on Mistral Large 4 into a selection of its customer services. The company has not disclosed exactly which services these are or when they will become available. It does, however, name two areas of application. In penetration testing and technical security assessments, the company expects AI to enable it to explore a wider range of attack scenarios. In incident investigation and incident response, it aims to use the technology to analyse digital traces more quickly and reconstruct how an attack unfolded.

Hugues Foulon, CEO of Orange Cyberdefense, says attacks are being organised on an ever larger scale and are increasingly automated. As a result, he argues, defences must also be able to scale. He identifies scale, speed and trust as the three challenges facing cybersecurity now that AI is being used more widely. Foulon says the model is trained by Orange Cyberdefense’s experts and used under their supervision. The company combines the AI with the knowledge of its teams and its own Cyber Threat Intelligence.

### Oversight and control

Orange Cyberdefense states that additional security requirements apply to these applications. These include measures for access management and the logging of AI activity. In addition, the models are tested for security risks. According to the company, security specialists always maintain oversight and remain responsible for all critical actions.

Orange Cyberdefense’s practical experience will be used to further develop the model for cybersecurity. In doing so, both companies aim to develop AI-assisted security capabilities that are auditable and remain under European control.

### European infrastructure

The European origin of the technology plays a central role in the partnership. Mistral AI develops its models in Europe and operates its own data centres in Europe. Orange Cyberdefense will run the AI models on computing capacity within Europe. According to the companies, this allows them to retain control over the technology and the environment in which it is used. They are primarily targeting organisations that want to use AI in sensitive environments and have requirements regarding digital sovereignty.

Marjorie Janiewicz, CRO of Mistral AI, says both companies share the same goal. According to Janiewicz, they want to offer European organisations a sovereign AI solution that is developed and managed in Europe.

### Not an exclusive choice

The partnership does not mean Orange Cyberdefense is committing to a single technology supplier. The company says it will remain independent in its choice of technology. It selects solutions based on customer needs, for example in the areas of data protection, laws and regulations, and digital resilience.

Orange Cyberdefense provides managed security services and detection and response services to organisations worldwide. The company says it employs more than 250 researchers and analysts and operates 16 SOCs.

# CERN and Mistral partner to build AI foundation models for physics

## It is meant to replace some specialised ‌algorithms now used to reconstruct ​and identify particles

Updated  - October 18, 2026 07:19 am IST

Reuters

[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)  Remove

File photo of Mistral AI, the French artificial intelligence company. File | Photo Credit: Reuters

European physics ‌research centre CERN and Mistral AI ​have signed a ⁠statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership to develop ‌foundation models for scientific discovery, the two organisations ‌said on Thursday (October 15, 2026).

The partners ‌aim ⁠to build a “Large Physics ⁠Model”, which CERN said in a statement would be the first foundation ​model for collider ‌physics, trained on billions of simulated particle collisions.

It is meant to replace some specialised ‌algorithms now used to reconstruct ​and identify particles.

CERN holds about one exabyte, or ⁠one million terabytes, of experimental data from the Large Hadron ‌Collider, and expects the volume of collisions to increase tenfold after its ongoing upgrade, expected around 2030.

“High-energy physics provides a unique environment ‌in which artificial intelligence can be developed ​and tested with exceptional rigour,” CERN Chief Information ⁠Officer Enrica Porcari said.

No timeline or ⁠budget was disclosed. Both sides said the models could ‌later serve other sciences.
